business.description: GOCL Corporation Limited operates as an integrated Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) provider delivering end-to-end solutions across the product lifecycle, and focuses on unlocking value from strategically located real estate assets. The company is pursuing entry into the energy sector through the proposed acquisition of Hinduja National Power Corporation Limited (HNPCL).

outlook.statement: The proposed acquisition of HNPCL is expected to enhance the Company's operational scale, strengthen the resilience of its cash flows, and position GOCL to participate in India's expanding power ecosystem, while creating a strong platform for long-term shareholder value creation.

Thermal capacity requirement by 2034-35 is estimated at approximately 3,07,000 MW against 2,11,855 MW installed capacity as on 31.03.2023. Rising peak demand and policy tailwinds in India have renewed interest in thermal generation.
The Board will continue to strengthen the businesses that define the future while pursuing new avenues that complement the portfolio and broaden capabilities.

GOCL-EMS aims to strengthen its position as an Original Design Manufacturing (ODM) solutions provider by moving up the value chain from manufacturing to product design and engineering services. Key priorities include increasing local value addition, developing indigenous product designs, expanding into high-growth sectors such as industrial electronics, defence, IOT, Automotive and e-Mobility, and leveraging India's growing electronics ecosystem.

HNPCL offers significant long-term growth potential through a planned 600 MW brownfield expansion. The existing large project site and coastal location also offer long-term options for FGD retrofits and ammonia/hydrogen pilot co-firing. The plant has a residual life of over 20 years, reasonable cost per MW, established infrastructure, and good payback visibility under stable operations.

The Company is in the process of early monetization of the 'ecopolis' project by sale of the entire project. The OWO project in London, UK is receiving good response and holds potential for shareholders' value.

Indian economy projected to grow at 6.6% in FY 2026-27 driven by strong domestic fundamentals and continued policy support. EMS business benefited from India's strong electronics manufacturing momentum driven by PLI-led investments, expansion of domestic component ecosystem, semiconductor initiatives, increasing exports, and Make in India program.
Outlook and plans have been mentioned in the Board's Report.

The Board of Directors approved a 'Scheme of Merger by Absorption' of Hinduja National Power Corporation Limited (HNPCL) with and into the Company with appointed date of April 1, 2025, subject to requisite statutory and regulatory approvals and sanction of the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). The Company has received no objection letters from the Stock Exchanges.

The Company entered into an Agreement to Sell on March 27, 2026 with the SPVs of Tata Realty and Infrastructure Limited for the sale of the Company's property situated at Yelahanka, Bengaluru, known as 'Ecopolis' for approximately Rs 81,500 lakhs. The Company received an advance of Rs 100 lakhs during the year.

Environmental and operational risks may result in regulatory penalties, operational disruptions, increased costs and reputational impact. Delays in obtaining approvals and licences may affect project timelines and business expansion.
The Company may encounter intense competition from both domestic and international players.
The Company is exposed to the risk of delays or shortfalls in loan recoveries, which may adversely affect cash flows, asset quality, profitability, and capital deployment.

Prolonged or unforeseen litigation, including tax and regulatory disputes, may adversely affect the Company's performance and reputation. Such proceedings may lead to financial penalties, operational disruptions and management distraction.
The integration of technology into the Company's operations increases its exposure to cybersecurity threats and IT failures.
Geopolitical frictions and strategic trade restrictions continue to fragment global freight routes. Delays in multi-modal transport corridors slow down the movement of critical industrial parts.
Rising cost of doing business due to rising wages, labour inflation, logistics and raw materials in key manufacturing regions.
Sub-par rainfall and the El Niño effect place severe stress on thermal power plants by causing acute cooling water shortages.
